BiblicalUsage: Patiyr is open, unoccupied, free. It appears once, in 1 Chronicles 9:33, where the singers, chief of the fathers of the Levites, remain in the chambers and are free from other service, because they are employed in that work day and night.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the singers were free from other work so they could do the one work, and freedom from service is sometimes the way God keeps a servant at his post.
